postfactus , or separate, post fac-tus , a, um, Part., from the obsol. postfacio,
I.made or done afterwards (post-class.): “post facta furta (opp. ante facta),” Gell. 17, 7, 3 .— Absol. : “ex postfacto,” from what is done afterwards, afterwards, subsequently, Dig. 21, 1, 44 fin. (20, 1, 22).
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
